newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to cut sulphur content in fuel oil.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to cut sulphur content in fuel oil.

text.p: South Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy said on Monday the sulphur content in fuel oil would be reduced from July 1 in line with tougher laws on the environment.

The sulphur content in fuel oil would be reduced to 0.5 percent from 1.0 percent from July 1 in urban areas, ministry officials said. The reduction would be extended to most cities and counties from July 1, 1999.

A maximum of 0.1 percent sulphur content in diesel, which is used as an industrial fuel as well as for home heating, would be enforced throughout the country from July 1. It is currently fixed at a maximum of 0.1 percent for most cities and counties.
The sulphur content in diesel for cars would be lowered to a maximum of 0.05 percent in April 1998, from the current 0.1 percent. --Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5643
